messages:
maya: FYI repro in the Kotlin sample app — when you hit back/rotate quickly during a multipart upload the server sees duplicate parts (two POSTs). Not happening in the Java sample.

alex: can you paste a minimal repro and logs? curious if this is our retry logic or okhttp behaviour.

maya: repro steps in the branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/tree/bug/multipart-dup-upload-kotlin - run SampleUploadActivity, pick a large file, press back while upload progress ~10-30%. Server logs show two distinct POST bodies.

maya: logs: ```
I/Upload: starting upload id=42
I/OkHttp: http request-> POST /upload  (content-length: unknown)
W/Network: write failed - socket closed by peer
I/OkHttp: retrying request (retryOnConnectionFailure)
I/Upload: completed upload id=42
```

simon: that stack looks like okhttp is retrying and RequestBody can't be replayed so it ends up streaming partial then restarting (server sees a second full upload when the network allowed it). Java sample probably uses a FileRequestBody with known content-length so okhttp rewinds; Kotlin sample uses streaming/requestbody-from-sink helper that isn't repeatable.

chloe: this smells like SDK parity: our Kotlin helper for RequestBody differs from Java. Also note Retrofit's suspend adapter cancels the coroutine which calls `call.cancel()` vs enqueue callback flow — cancellation timing differs and may interact with retry.

alex: workaround for now: disable connection retries for the client used by the upload repo: ```java
new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
  .callTimeout(Duration.ofMinutes(5))
  .build();
```

alex: if body isn't repeatable, disable retry or buffer the body (e.g., write to tmp file and use FileRequestBody) so okhttp can retry safely.

maya: confirmed disabling retry stops duplicates on my device. But we need a proper fix — either make Kotlin RequestBody repeatable or detect streaming bodies and avoid retrying.

simon: other idea: set `RequestBody.isOneShot()` semantics — but thats bespoke. Simpler: update Kotlin helper to set content-length when possible and fallback to buffering for small files. Also add a note in DX docs about lifecycle cancellation differences between suspend/callback.

chloe: I'll open a PR that: 1) updates the Kotlin RequestBody implementation to buffer small uploads (<=2MB) and set content-length when possible, 2) adds a sample toggle `okhttp.disableRetries` for testing, 3) adds a test in sample-apps verifying no duplicate POSTs on onPause/cancel.

maya: thanks @chloe — also adding repro steps to the onboarding guide so new engs who hit this know to try disabling retries first.

ci-bot: CI: build passed for branch bug/multipart-dup-upload-kotlin (jobs: unit-tests, lint).

alex: long-term: consider aligning default SDK client configs across Java/Kotlin samples (same retryOnConnectionFailure default, timeouts). This will reduce these parity surprises.

maya: action items: maya -> add server capture test; chloe -> PR for buffering + sample toggle; simon -> quick doc note about suspend cancellation nuance. I'll follow up in the PR with logs and device traces. :+1:

alex: sounds good. Thanks for catching this early — this would've bubbled up in the field.
